title: PM Fils-Aimé Tells Special UN Meeting Haitians 'Can Wait No Longer' as GSF Renewal Vote Looms
detail: Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé addressed a special UN meeting on the future of security in Haiti on September 24, 2026, saying "There is a people. A people who can wait no longer. A people waiting to regain security, to return home to work, to send their children to school, and to freely choose their leaders." He said Haiti's next government "must come through the ballot box" since "voting restores legitimacy," and confirmed general elections remain scheduled for December 13, 2026, with electoral operations launched, citizens registering, and political organizations already certified. He also linked security gains to combating "the illicit flows that fuel violence." UN Special Representative Carlos Ruiz Massieu and ECOSOC President Amar Bendjama also spoke. The meeting underscored the strained state of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) ahead of the Security Council's expected September 30 vote on renewing its mandate: the force counted only 1,083 deployed personnel against a 5,500-person authorized ceiling, while 6.4 million Haitians require humanitarian assistance and nearly 1.5 million remain internally displaced.

title: Haitian Advocacy Groups Demand Answers Over $780,000 Roger Stone Lobbying Contract
detail: Filings published by the U.S. Department of Justice on September 16, 2026 revealed that Haiti's Foreign Ministry, under Foreign Minister Raina Forbin, signed a $780,000-a-year lobbying contract on September 2, 2026 with Drake Ventures LLC, the firm of Trump ally Roger Stone — $65,000 a month, billed as $195,000 quarterly installments with the first due on signature, automatically renewing and non-cancellable by Haiti for 12 months, with a mandate limited to advocating on "those issues the Client deems necessary and appropriate." The Haitian American Foundation for Democracy (HAFFD) publicly demanded answers on September 24, 2026, describing Stone as "the Trump confidant convicted of lying to Congress" and a "founding architect of the mass-deportation movement," and noting the contract makes no mention of Temporary Protected Status, deportations, or the safety of Haitians in the U.S. — even though roughly 330,000-350,000 Haitians had lost TPS protections weeks earlier and deportation flights to Cap-Haïtien had resumed. HAFFD gave the Haitian government 15 days to explain the contract's purpose and Stone's selection, and said it would share the response with Congress. Haiti separately pays another Trump-aligned lobbying firm $35,000 a month.
